name: MA-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 11 points and incumbent Lori Trahan is running for re-election
Overwhelming fundraising gap: Trahan has $1.8 million on hand versus about $6,600 for Gary Grossi
Prediction markets price the race at roughly 96% Democratic
No polls, expert ratings, or outside spending signal any competitiveness
model.rationale: The district's Democratic lean, Trahan's incumbency, and a fundraising advantage of more than 200-to-1 all point the same way, and markets price the race as safely Democratic. With no polling or ratings suggesting a contest, the only real question is the size of the margin.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending for Grossi or a sharp national backlash against Democrats could narrow the margin, though neither would likely threaten the outcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Massachusetts' third district leans Democratic by about eleven points, and incumbent Lori Trahan is seeking another term with every structural advantage. She has raised roughly $1.8 million and holds nearly all of it on hand, while Republican Gary Grossi has raised under $10,000. No outside spending has appeared on either side, and no general-election polls have been conducted in the race.

Prediction markets price Trahan's chances at about 96 percent, and the fundamentals point the same direction: district lean, incumbency, and a lopsided money gap. An independent candidate is on the ballot but shows no fundraising footprint. The race is rated Safe Democratic, with the main uncertainty being the size of Trahan's winning margin rather than the outcome itself.
